beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evidence, uncertainty, and correction history would become easier to inspect and update separately.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also considers paying for correction and supporting a portfolio of approaches.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These are institutional proposals whose costs and unwanted effects still need evaluation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their purpose is to make disagreement actionable without requiring a verdict on an entire career.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial intelligence enters the argument as a possible way to reduce some assessment costs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It might assist comparison, evidence tracing, consistency checks, or continuing review.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book does not treat an automated score as a sovereign scientific verdict.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The same machinery can reproduce status bias or create another opaque authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its role therefore depends on visible procedures and meaningful opportunities for human challenge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This restraint matters to the book's broader argument about distributing trust without disguising power.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later proposals explore pedigree sensitivity, portable evidence, and confidence that changes with new information.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A counterfactual audit can ask whether altered identity signals change an assessment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Such sensitivity alone does not prove discrimination in every individual decision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book combines diagnostic tools with procedures for challenge, revision, and justified surprise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It also asks whether new guardians of evidence could become gatekeepers themselves.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading these limits is essential to evaluating the reforms rather than merely admiring their intentions.
